Hridi Haq’s ‘1971 Shei Shob Din’ release date announced
2023-05-30T12:34:11+06:00 | Arts & Entertainment Desk
https://www.thedailystar.net/entertainment/tv-film/news/hridi-haqs-1971-shei-shob-din-release-date-announced-3333256

Noted actress and playwright Hridi Haq is all set to make her directorial debut with the much anticipated government-granted film, "1971 Shei Shob Din", which depicts the gripping narrative of Bangladesh's Liberation War.

A homage to Bangla cinema’s golden era, with hand-painted art

On Monday night, during a press event held at the National Art Gallery of Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy, the talented director unveiled the much-awaited release date. With excitement, she announced that the film will be released on August 18.

The event was graced by the presence of esteemed personalities such as Lucky Inam, Mamunur Rashid, Jayanta Chattopadhyay, Tauquir Ahmed, Ferdous, Sara Zaker, Abul Hayat, Litu Anam, Tanzika Amin and many others, who have played vital roles in the film.

Director Hridi Haq expressed her meticulous approach towards the movie, stating, "We have invested great care and effort into creating this film. Now, we eagerly await the moment when it can be presented to the audience. If all goes well, '1971 Shei Shob Din' will grace the silver screen on August 18."

Hridi Haq’s ‘1971 Shei Shob Din’ shines a light on Bangladesh’s independence

The film revolves around a family's experiences during 1971, providing a poignant portrayal of the era.

Apart from directing, Hridi Haq herself features in "1971 Shei Shob Din", alongside a talented ensemble cast comprising Mamunur Rashid, Jayanta Chattopadhyay, Munmun Ahmed, Shilpi Sharkar Apu, Ferdous, Tareen, Litu Anam, Saju Khadem, Sanjida Preeti, and many more. Notably, Litu Anam makes a remarkable comeback to cinema with this film, after a hiatus of 15 years.

Srijit Mukherji calls rumours of divorce with Mithila ‘baseless’

In the movie, Ferdous, Litu Anam, and Sajal deliver compelling performances, portraying the roles of three brothers actively engaged in the Liberation War.
